answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists sybil attacks by making each identity costly: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a cedar taking root in a grove — one tree, one plot of soil. A single operator spawning thousands of fake agents must fund each one, so the attack's cost grows linearly while its payoff stays flat. Misbehavior slashes the deposit, and the forfeited funds flow back into the shared pool, like a river returning water to the ocean. Honest agents eventually reclaim their stake, so the barrier deters fakes without taxing real participants.
